title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（金野武司研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Konno Takeshi)
teachers:
KONNO Takeshi
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: Training will be carried out to grow up engineers in the information technology fields with problem-finding ability, solution ability, and application ability through educational programs that emphasize basic knowledge and skills in the fields of information technology engineering, which are highly important in modern society. The common research theme is "intentional communication" and issues related to the artificial realization of these themes should be widely covered.
advice:
Each participant has a project theme and works independently or as a group. Meetings are held as closely as necessary, and activities are reported in weekly reports. The activities required for the first semester and the second semester are as follows:

・First semester : Decide on the project themes to be implemented and submit project proposals. The progress of activities is announced at an interim conference held at the end of the semester.
・Second semester : At the end of the semester, the results of the activities are compiled into a project report, which is then presented at a open presentation review meeting. The handover is made to the next year's students.

This course is the last subject in the project design, and it is positioned as a course which integrates the matters learned in all courses. The aim is to review basic courses and acquire advanced specialized knowledge through experiment and theoretical examination of project themes.
books: Reference books：Human: The Science Behind What Makes Us Unique [Ecco], The Cultural Origins of Human Cognition [Harvard University Press], Constructing a Language: A Usage-Based Theory of Language Acquisition [Harvard University Press]
requiredKnowledge:
1.A constant questioning of "Why?" about all the actions you take in an activity.
2.While holding many discussions with teaching staff, seniors and classmates, always take the attitude of co-creating "something new" in those discussions and respect each other's ideas.
3.To have an attitude to discover and acquire the knowledge and technology necessary for solving problems by oneself, and to positively utilize laboratory and laboratory facilities, LC, and YUMEKOBO.

activityGoals.body: Be able to clarify the purpose of the project, to grasp the content, and to draft the research plan.
Be able to promote the project through the communication with project members and teachers.
Be able to solve problems and tasks in the project execution by oneself.
Be able to summarize the activity results into the project report.
Be able to explain the contents of the project and effectively present the results of activities.

achievementLevels.ideal: Participants can fully understand the objectives of the project, develop a detailed annual plan, and explain the objectives and plans to others in an easy-to-understand manner. The results of the project can be compiled into a project report, which can be published as an extramural submission such as a research paper. In addition, participants can participate in research activities outside the university, such as academic conferences, and make presentations and receive high evaluations.
achievementLevels.standard: Participants can understand the objectives of the project, develop an annual plan, and fully explain the objectives and the plan to others. The results of the project can be summarized in a project report, which can be presented to the open presentation review meeting for full evaluation.

              Training will be carried out to grow up engineers in the information technology fields with problem-finding ability, solution ability, and application ability through educational programs that emphasize basic knowledge and skills in the fields of information technology engineering, which are highly important in modern society. The common research theme is "intentional communication" and issues related to the artificial realization of these themes should be widely covered.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Each participant has a project theme and works independently or as a group. Meetings are held as closely as necessary, and activities are reported in weekly reports. The activities required for the first semester and the second semester are as follows:

・First semester : Decide on the project themes to be implemented and submit project proposals. The progress of activities is announced at an interim conference held at the end of the semester.
・Second semester : At the end of the semester, the results of the activities are compiled into a project report, which is then presented at a open presentation review meeting. The handover is made to the next year's students.

This course is the last subject in the project design, and it is positioned as a course which integrates the matters learned in all courses. The aim is to review basic courses and acquire advanced specialized knowledge through experiment and theoretical examination of project themes.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Reference books：Human: The Science Behind What Makes Us Unique [Ecco], The Cultural Origins of Human Cognition [Harvard University Press], Constructing a Language: A Usage-Based Theory of Language Acquisition [Harvard University Press]

3.To have an attitude to discover and acquire the knowledge and technology necessary for solving problems by oneself, and to positively utilize laboratory and laboratory facilities, LC, and YUMEKOBO.
